--- title: "Module 2: The tidyverse" ---
![](../../src/images/hex_complex.png){.intro_image fig-alt="Logo"} Module 2 introduces the tidyverse tools that you will use for most of your data work in R. You will learn to subset and extract data, create and modify variables, perform grouped operations, reshape and join data frames, build plots with *ggplot2*, identify and repair untidy data, and replace repeated statements with iteration. Complete Preliminary lessons 1-4 and Module 1 before beginning this module. ## Module overview - **2.1 Introduction to subsetting and extraction**: Distinguish subsetting from extraction, then select appropriate tools for obtaining rows, columns, values, and metadata. - **2.2 Introduction to mutation**: Create new columns and modify existing columns with *dplyr*. - **2.3 Grouped operations and summarizing**: Apply mutation, subsetting, and summary operations within groups, then distinguish per-operation grouping from persistent grouping. - **2.4 Reshaping data frames**: Combine and split columns and tables, join tables by shared keys, and reshape data between long and wide forms. - **2.5 Introduction to data visualization with ggplot2**: Build plots by specifying data, aesthetic mappings, geometries, scales, and labels. An optional introductory video is included. - **2.6 Tidy data**: Apply the three rules of tidy data to identify and repair structural problems in a messy dataset. - **2.7 Iteration with purrr**: Apply one operation to every element of a list or vector with the *purrr* map functions: read every file in a folder, build and save a plot for each species, and read each file with its own settings. **Problem set**: [Problem set 2: Counting coqui frogs](../../problem_sets/problem_set_2/problem_set_2.qmd) *Complete the lessons in order because later lessons build on earlier ones.* ## About this module's data In this module, we will use the following data files in our exercises: **`angola_ungulates.rds`**: These data are formatted as a list of two tibble data frames and represent all observations of ungulates in Angola by the iNaturalist community science project. I downloaded these data using the R package *rinat*. Taxonomic information for the observed species were obtained from the [Integrated Taxonomic Information System (ITIS)](https://www.itis.gov/){target="_blank"} and downloaded using the R package *taxize*. **`chickadees.csv`**: This file includes measures of Carolina and Black-capped chickadees across several regions of the United States. The data were collected by the Smithsonian [Neighborhood Nestwatch](https://nationalzoo.si.edu/migratory-birds/neighborhood-nestwatch){target="_blank"} program, a community science project. Measurements taken include the species of bird, mass, wing length, and sex. **`district_birds.rds`**: This is a tidy dataset that contains a subset of records from the Smithsonian Migratory Bird Center's [Neighborhood Nestwatch](https://nationalzoo.si.edu/migratory-birds/neighborhood-nestwatch){target="_blank"} (NN) program. NN is a community science project where scientists visit backyards, neighborhoods, and schools to conduct bird banding demonstrations and sample bird populations. The data include tables for sites, visits, point counts, and capture events, and a table that provides natural history information for observed birds. Geographic coordinate values have been jittered to protect the privacy of NN participants. **`spotted_lanternfly.rds`**: This is a tabular dataset of [iNaturalist observations of spotted lanternfly (*Lycorma delicatula*)](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/spotted-lanternfly){target="_blank"}, an invasive pest species whose spread is of commercial and ecological concern. Each row is an observation submitted by a community science participant via a web or smartphone application. **`untidy_data.rds`**: These are "fake" data (though subsets of "real" data!) that I am using for illustration purposes in the tidy data lesson. **`weather_tidy.rds`**: These data are formatted as a list of two tibble data frames that represent the normalized (i.e., tidy data) version of `messy_weather.csv`. The data were collected from 2010-2020 at five NOAA weather stations located in California, North Carolina, New York, and Wisconsin, and contain measures of precipitation, snow, and temperatures during the month of March. ## Readings and resources :::{style="margin-top:16px;"} - Wickham & Grolemund (1^st^ edition): - [5.1-5.5: Data transformation](https://r4ds.had.co.nz/transform.html#transform){target="_blank"} - [5.6: Grouped summaries](https://r4ds.had.co.nz/transform.html?q=group#grouped-summaries-with-summarise){target="_blank"} - [12.1-12.5: Tidy data](https://r4ds.had.co.nz/tidy-data.html){target="_blank"} - [Wickham, H. 2014. Tidy data. *Journal of Statistical Software* 59: 1-23.](https://vita.had.co.nz/papers/tidy-data.pdf){target="_blank"} - Chang, W. 2019. [R Graphics Cookbook](https://r-graphics.org/){target="_blank"}. O'Reilly Media, Inc., Sebastopol CA. - Wickham H, D Navarro, and TL Pedersen. 2021. [ggplot2: Elegant Graphics for Data Analysis](https://ggplot2-book.org/index.html){target="_blank"}. Springer-Verlag, New York NY. - **Cheat sheets:** I *strongly* recommend printing the cheat sheets to have a handy reference to tidyverse functions and how they are used (*Note: Please see the [translated cheat sheets](https://rstudio.github.io/cheatsheets/translations.html){target="_blank"} if you would prefer a language other than English*)! - [Data tidying (tidyr)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rstudio/cheatsheets/main/tidyr.pdf){target="_blank"} - [Data transformation (dplyr)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rstudio/cheatsheets/main/data-transformation.pdf){target="_blank"} - [Data visualization (ggplot)](https://rstudio.github.io/cheatsheets/html/data-visualization.html){target="_blank"} ::: ## Reference ::: panel - **Aesthetic mappings**: How the data are mapped to visual attributes. - **Arguments**: A value supplied to a function that modifies its behavior when the function runs. - **Assignment (noun)**: A reference that R uses to call data from your computer’s memory (also called "name"). - **Assignment (verb)**: The act of associating a name with an object (typically to the global environment). - **Assignment operator**: A function used to assign an object to a name. - **Atomic vector**: A one-dimensional, homogeneous data object (a set of values of the same class). - **Attributes**: Information about the values of an object that is not contained in the values themselves. - **Body**: The set of instructions inside the function (determines what happens when you run a function). - **Character**: A symbol or set of symbols from a given alphabet (note: also includes numbers and punctuation). - **Child**: An object whose name is stored as a reference in a parent object. - **Class**: A blueprint that describes an object's structure. - **Code section**: A portion of an R script file that is delineated by a section header. - **Compound key**: A set of variables in a data frame that, combined, represent the primary key of a table. - **Console pane**: A pane of RStudio used for interactively running R commands and viewing their output. - **Coordinate system**: The projection of the data in a plot (e.g., x and y Cartesian coordinates). - **Coordinate system (in ggplot)**: Projection of data (e.g., x and y Cartesian coordinates). - **Coordinate system (in GIS)**: A model that can be used to locate data on the surface of the Earth. - **Core tidyverse package**: Packages that are attached with `library(tidyverse)`. - **csv file**: A file stored in the "comma separated values" format. This describes a plain text file where commas separate values and each record (e.g., row in a data frame) is placed on a new line. - **Data**: The information being plotted. - **Data cleaning**: Correcting the content of a dataset -- classes, units, misspellings, impossible values, and missing data codes -- as opposed to tidying, which corrects its structure. - **Data frame**: A two-dimensional, heterogeneous data object comprised of equal-length vectors (a restrictive type of list under-the-hood). - **Data object**: Containers for values that structure references in an ordered, predictable way. - **Dimensions**: The arrangement of values in an object; may also refer to the number of values or child objects within a given dimension (i.e., rows or columns) - **Double numeric vector**: An atomic numeric vector where the values are stored as decimal numbers (essentially). - **Environment**: A dimensionless data structure that contains references (names) to data stored in memory. - **Environment (of a function)**: The location of a function's variables. - **Escape character**: A backslash (`\`) placed before a character to tell R to treat that character literally rather than as part of R's syntax. - **Experimental**: A function currently being tested for permanent distribution in a package (these functions are usually, but not always, safe to use). - **Extraction**: Returning a child object from within its parent object, or returning part of an object such as its names or class -- as opposed to subsetting, which returns an object of the parent's class. - **Facets**: Subsets of data within a given plot (i.e., plots are broken into subplots based on some grouping variable). - **Factor**: A value that maps character labels onto integers. - **Filter**: Subset data by logical condition. - **Filtering**: The process of subsetting a data frame's rows by a logical condition, most often with `filter()`. - **Foreign key**: A variable in a data frame that refers to the primary key of another data frame. - **Formals**: Arguments within a function. - **Function**: A set of instructions (stored as an R object) used to complete a given task. - **Global environment**: A workspace that provides a reference point for all user-assigned objects associated with the current session. - **Heterogeneous object**: A container that holds values of one or more object classes. - **Homogeneity**: Whether an object may contain one or more than one class of object. - **Homogeneous object**: a container that holds values of only one class. - **Index**: The location of a value or component object within a parent object. This term can also be used as a verb to describe the process of indexing. - **Indexing**: The process of subsetting an object by the position (location) of a value or component within it. - **Infix function**: A function in which the name of the function is placed between the function's arguments. - **Install**: Download the data and functions from a package onto your computer. - **Integer**: A whole number, or an atomic vector of data stored as whole numbers. - **Iteration or Iterate**: The repeating of a given process a set number of times. - **Key**: A variable in a data frame that is used to identify unique records. - **Labels**: Character values supplied to the labels argument of factor() to rename the levels as a factor is created. - **Lambda**: An anonymous function created for a temporary task, written as `\(x) ...`, where `x` stands for the element being handled. - **Layers**: Expression of the data in the plot. - **Layers (geometries)**: The expression of the data in a plot (e.g., points, bars, or lines). - **Level of observation**: The kind of thing that is being measured (e.g., a station, or a day at a station). Every level of observation forms a table. - **Levels**: The character values mapped to a factor's integer values. - **Library**: The location of a package on your computer. - **List**: A one-dimensional, heterogeneous data object that can hold values or objects of any class. - **List item**: A data object contained within a list. - **Logical constant**: `TRUE` or `FALSE`. - **Logical operator**: An operator used to test a logical statement (e.g., `3 > 2`). - **Matrix**: A two-dimensional, homogeneous data object arranged into rows and columns (an atomic vector under-the-hood). - **Memory**: A temporary storage location for instructions (functions) and data. - **Metadata**: Descriptive information that provides crucial summary details about a data object. For geospatial data, this should always include the coordinate reference system! - **Metapackage**: A package that is comprised of more than one smaller packages. - **Mutation**: The process of adding columns to a data frame and/or modifying existing columns (or adding/modifying list items to/in a list). - **Name**: A symbol that R evaluates to retrieve the object associated with it through a binding in an environment. - **Negated selection**: The use of the negative symbol (`-`) or, more recently, the *not* operator (`!`) to select all columns *except* the supplied column or columns. - **Nested function**: A function that is run inside of another function. - **Object**: A collection of one or more values or functions. - **Observation**: The full set of values measured on the same observational unit across attributes. - **Observational unit**: The kind of thing that is being measured -- Wickham's term for what these lessons call a level of observation. - **One-dimensional object**: Objects where data are arranged in a single line. - **Operator**: A function expressed that is expressed as a symbol and is not followed by parentheses. - **Order**: The position of values (or child objects) within a data object. - **Package**: A set of pre-written functions that can be downloaded (*note: There are also data packages!*) - **Package environment**: A collection of variable names associated with objects in a package. - **Parent**: An object or environment that contains references to other objects. - **Placeholder symbol**: In the context of piping, the symbol that defines the location in the right-hand-side function where the piped data will be inserted (a period, `.`, for the *magrittr* pipe). - **Prefix function**: A function in which the name of the function precedes the target of the evaluation. - **Primary key**: A variable in a data frame that is used to identify unique records. - **Primitive function**: A function written in C code and made available to use through the base R package. - **Project**: A collection of files that is referenced by a `.RProj` file. - **R session**: A running R process and its current state. - **RDS file**: A storage format for data sets that are written in, and written for, program R. - **Recursive assignments**: Names within a data object (a list or data frame), as opposed to names within the global environment. - **Recursive object**: An object made up of references to other, nested objects (e.g., a list). - **Reference tree**: A visualization of the storage locations and names of parent and child objects. - **Relative file path**: The path to a file on your hard drive relative to the current working directory. - **Scales**: Maps from data to aesthetic space. - **Script**: A text file that contains a set of commands to read, manipulate, and analyze data. - **Session**: The time spent and operations conducted since opening R. - **Session history**: All lines of code that have been sent to R since the beginning of a session (or since the session history was last cleared). - **Side effect**: A change that a function makes outside of the object that it returns, such as writing a file to disk. - **Snake_case**: A naming convention in which all letters are lowercase and words are separated with an underscore (`_`). - **Source pane**: A pane of RStudio used for writing, editing, and running scripts. - **String**: A character value comprised of more than one symbol. - **Structure**: The dimensionality, homogeneity, and storage class of a data object (may also describe its metadata). - **Subset**: The process of reducing the number of items in a list (including columns in a data frame!), rows in a data frame, or values in an atomic vector. - **Subsetting**: Reduce a data object to a component or components of interest. - **Summarize**: The process of calculating a summary statistic, or multiple summary statistics of a data frame and returning the resultant data as a tibble data frame. - **Superseded**: A function for which a new function or argument has been added to a package (these functions should typically be avoided). - **Tab**: Each pane has a tab on the top of it. For example, I will often refer to the Environment or History tabs of the workspace pane. - **Theme**: Styling of non-data elements in a plot. - **Tibble**: A type of data frame with additional properties that make it especially useful. - **Tidy data**: A data format developed by Hadley Wickham (based on Codd's rules) in which every row represents an observation, every column represents a variable, and every level of observation represents a table. - **Transitive dependence**: A relationship in which the values in one column can be determined by the values in another column, so that the same fact is recorded in two places. - **Two-dimensional object**: An object where data are arranged as rows and columns. - **Type**: How an object is stored in your computer. - **Value**: A single recorded entry in a dataset. - **Variable**: The full set of values that measure the same underlying attribute across observational units. - **Vector**: A one-dimensional object. - **Version history**: Changes to a package since its inception. - **Viewer pane**: A pane of RStudio used for navigating your system's files, viewing help files, and images/plot output (and more) - **Workspace pane**: A pane of RStudio used to view/manage objects in your global environment and your session history. ::: ::: panel **Important!** Primitive functions, as well as functions in the packages that R attaches by default (e.g., *base*, *utils*, *stats*, and *graphics*), are available as soon as you start an R session. ::: function_table ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
